subject: System Design
title: DNS Record Types
description: A fast breakdown of DNS Record Types for builders.

hook.text: An A record maps a domain to an IP. A CNAME maps it to another domain. MX routes email. Each type serves a purpose.

buildup.text: DNS supports many record types: A for IPv4, AAAA for IPv6, CNAME for aliases, MX for mail, TXT for verification.

discovery.text: TXT records are used for email authentication (SPF, DKIM), domain verification, and service discovery.

twist.text: CNAME records can't coexist with other records at the zone apex. Many providers use ALIAS records as a workaround.

climax.text: Understanding DNS records is essential for setting up websites, email, load balancing, and service discovery.

punchline.text: Each DNS record type serves a specific purpose.

quiz.question: What does an MX record do?
options: Routes email to the correct mail server
Maps a domain to an IP address
